name: Ironmarrow Tactical Conceal Vest
description:
Ironmarrow is a street-level brand with a specific reputation: they make concealment gear that works, priced for people who can't afford Vanthorpe's civilian carry options but need the same function. The Tactical Conceal Vest looks, from the outside, like a plain athletic vest — the kind worn by Tier 2 workers who want an extra layer without a full jacket. Matte black or deep olive, smooth-faced synthetic shell, simple zip front. What the outside doesn't show is the interior: four flat concealment pockets distributed across the torso, reinforced with a light ballistic-grade panel at the chest that provides basic protection against low-velocity impacts. The pockets are sized for a compact sidearm, a blade, documents, or tech.

Ironmarrow sells through three locations in the Midmarket and via a referral-only network in the Shelf. They don't advertise. Their quality control is better than it has any right to be at this price point, which is why people trust them. The vest is worn by fixers, couriers, off-duty security, and anyone who has decided they need to carry something and can't afford to look like they are.
functionality: Integrated low-velocity ballistic protection at chest panel. Four interior concealment pockets with flat-profile construction. No electronics.
what_it_says: You're prepared for something. You'd prefer no one knew.
worn_by: Shelf residents who've been robbed before
people in situations where carrying openly is not an option
story_hooks: An Ironmarrow vest stopped a blade during an attempted mugging in Stack 3 last month. The owner survived. The story is circulating in the Shelf and Midmarket, and Ironmarrow's referral list has tripled. Someone with a vest company bigger than Ironmarrow's is paying attention.

A run of Ironmarrow vests from 2199 has interior pockets with a hidden fifth compartment that appears on no spec sheet. It's the right size for a data chip. Who added it, and to how many vests, is unknown.
Ironmarrow's founder is a former Vantablack contractor. No one is supposed to know this. Someone figured it out and is deciding what to do with the information.

physical_description.visual_profile: Deceptively minimal athletic vest with a clean, understated silhouette. From the front, indistinguishable from casual layerwear—the kind worn by Tier 2-3 workers for extra insulation under jackets or alone in summer. No visible logos, no tactical aesthetic. Reads as practical, not threatening. The interior tells a different story.
physical_description.fit: Slim but not tight; cut to layer cleanly over a standard shirt without bunching. Sits just above the hip, leaving torso mobility untouched. Designed to be unremarkable under a coat or worn solo without drawing attention.
physical_description.primary_material: Matte synthetic shell (likely recycled polyester blend or ballistic-weave composite), smooth-faced exterior with minimal texture. Interior lining is heavier-gauge, reinforced at chest and side panel zones.
physical_description.texture: Exterior: smooth, almost matte, with a slight friction grip to prevent sliding. Interior: subtle quilting where ballistic reinforcement runs; concealment pockets have discreet edge-binding to prevent snagging.
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte black (primary) or deep olive. No contrasting trim, no branding. Designed to vanish into any urban wardrobe.
physical_description.closures: Single-track metal zipper, matte-black finish, smooth pull. No visible snap points or tactical hardware. Zips fully from collar to hem.
distinctive_features: Four flat internal concealment pockets: two chest-width (compact sidearm or folded documents), two flank-positioned (blade sheath, tech module, or secondary storage)
Reinforced ballistic panel at chest—light-grade, stops low-velocity handgun rounds and shrapnel but not rifle fire
Zero external branding; Ironmarrow trust-mark is interior neck label only
Zippered access pockets designed so contents don't print through fabric
Slight structural padding at shoulders and chest that mimics athletic wear, not armor
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 functional. Priced for working-class carry. Signals practical street sense, not corporate wealth or sub-grade desperation.
physical_description.cultural_context: Street-level fixers, off-duty security personnel, couriers moving sensitive cargo, anyone who has decided discretion matters more than display. Worn by people with reasons but not spectacle. Marks the wearer as someone who thinks ahead without advertising it.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine to broken-in. Ironmarrow quality means it wears well. Most units show minimal fading after months of use. Worn seams are rare. The vest ages into its purpose rather than degrading.
